newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM Howard still losing support.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM Howard still losing support.

text.p: A fall in voter support for Australian Prime Minister John Howard and his conservative government, battered by race and corruption issues, has become entrenched, according to a newspaper poll published on Tuesday.
The Australian newspaper's Newspoll, a survey of 9,000 voters between April and June, found support for Howard amongst traditional conservative voters continuing to fall.
But Howard said he was not concerned by his government's falling popularity as it still held a strong lead over the Labor opposition.
"You can't have an indefinite honeymoon in politics," Howard told reporters in Townsville in the state of Queensland.

"We had a very long honeymoon. We've obviously been criticised fairly in some cases, unfairly on others on a number of issues over the past few months, and it's inevitable that you will go through these peaks and troughs," he said.
The Australian poll found voters were turning away from his Liberal-National coalition government and to minor parties such as the populist One Nation party.

It found government support in all states and age groups had fallen below that at the March 1996 election. The largest slumps were recorded in rural areas and from men and people over 50 -- the coalition's traditional support base.
But the Labor opposition was not gaining from the government's loss and its own support was also below that recorded at the 1996 election.
Primary support for the government fell to 43 percent from 47 percent at the 1996 election. Support for Labor dropped to 37 percent from 38.7 percent at the election.
Support for minor parties surged to a total of 20 percent from 14.3 percent at the 1996 election, with Hanson's One Nation recording six percent.
